What the numbers say

For the session of Thursday, October 15, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (26 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-on. SPY is above its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is sideways and realised volatility is in the calm band.

16 of 26 tickers (62%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 17 of 25 (68%) above their 200-day average. Above 55% is the breadth the model requires, together with the benchmark above its 50-day average and volatility not high, for a risk-on reading. On the day 15 rose and 11 fell; the median move was +0.27%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Healthcare had the strongest average move at +2.69% and Technology the weakest at −1.37%, a spread of 4.06 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 1.67 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

No ticker has a 14-day RSI at or below 30, and 2 at or above 70 (SHEL, COST). An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-10-14), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 46% to 62%, and the regime reading changed from mixed to risk-on.
